previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic pancreatitis, asthma, lipodermatosclerosis, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for fever, productive cough, and increased leg erythema. She was evaluated for possible infection, but imaging and labs showed no pneumonia, bacteremia, urinary tract infection, or influenza. A viral upper respiratory infection was diagnosed as the cause of her fever and respiratory symptoms. She also experienced transient headaches, which resolved with analgesics and were found to have no intracranial cause on CT. Neck swelling was noted but imaging showed no abscess or structural abnormality. Leg swelling improved with reinstitution of furosemide after missed doses. She remained afebrile throughout her stay, her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home on her baseline medications with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.

aspirin, iron, and minocycline were initially held given concern 
for pill esophagitis, but these were resumed on discharge.  The 
patient had a barium esophagram/upper GI series/small bowel

hiatal hernia, no significant retention in the valleculae or 
piriform sinuses, and normal relaxation of the
cricopharyngeus. Her odynophagia resolved prior to discharge, 
and she was tolerating both solids and liquids without

discharge.

included viral illness, achalasia, pancreatitis flare, gastric

seemed unlikely, given absence of fever or leukocytosis, and

lipase was WNL, suggesting pancreatitis unlikely.  There was no 
evidence of gastric outlet obstruction on EGD or BAS/UGI

primary peristaltic contractions in the esophagus, a small, 
axial
hiatal hernia, no significant retention in the valleculae or

cricopharyngeus.  The patient received IVF and anti-emetics, 
with improvement in symptoms.  Her diet was advanced as 
tolerated, and she did not have any recurrent emesis.  She was 
discharged to home with PCP and GI ___ once able to 
tolerate adequate PO intake.
